- Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, with over 10,000 infections since May, making it the second-deadliest Ebola epidemic in history. The Bundibugyo strain is responsible, and there are no vaccines or approved treatments for this strain. Late case detection, ongoing armed conflict, and overwhelmed health services have fueled faster spread, with transmission reaching eight of the country’s 26 provinces and many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. The outbreak remains difficult to control. article.articleHeadline: Rio de Janeiro City Hall investigates new death due to suspected Mpox.
article.articleSummary:
- As of 30 October 2026, Rio de Janeiro City Hall is investigating a new death suspected to be caused by Mpox. In the last month, the city recorded 43 Mpox cases, with 2026 total cases already 77% higher than for all of 2025. The state health secretariat acknowledges the rise in cases but says it is not yet possible to declare an epidemic. Concurrently, patients report difficulties obtaining Mpox vaccine doses at municipal health centers.
- Rio de Janeiro reported 45 mpox (monkeypox) cases in September 2026, per the Municipal Health Secretariat. The city says the numbers remain under control and within the expected fluctuation since 2022. Notably, December 2023 peaked at 46 cases for the year. Mpox transmission occurs mainly through prolonged close contact with lesions or bodily fluids of infected individuals, and via contaminated objects such as recently handled surfaces, towels, bedding, or personal utensils. Prevention is emphasized as the key measure to curb viral spread. In the public network, treatment is supportive clinical care, focused on symptom relief, prevention of complications, and avoidance of dermatological or systemic sequelae. The report underscores ongoing local surveillance and routine monitoring.

article.articleHeadline: Paying for India's typhoid burden
article.articleSummary: 4.9 million typhoid fever cases and 7,850 deaths in India in 2023, with more than 80% of hospitalisations involving fluoroquinolone-resistant infections. Economic burden estimated at ₹12,300 crore, and about 70,000 households face catastrophic health spending; children under 10 account for over half of the economic impact. Urban, low-income settlements bear substantially higher risk, with incidence in urban children 576–1,173 per 100,000 child-years versus 35 in rural sites. Typhoid, caused by Salmonella typhi, presents with high fever lasting weeks, abdominal pain, diarrhoea and vomiting; untreated cases may perforate the gut or cause systemic complications. Transmission via contaminated food and water requires public action beyond individual precautions. Typhoid conjugate vaccine shows 79–85% protection in trials in Nepal, Malawi and Bangladesh, and India’s UIP inclusion was recommended in 2022. WHO’s Aug 2026 guidance supports vaccination in high-incidence or drug-resistant settings; India’s manufacturing capacity enables rollout, with a phased approach in high-burden districts. Vaccination could reduce treatment costs and preserve earnings, outweighing vaccine costs as part of public investment.

article.articleHeadline: Mouse models anchor Chandipura virus research as vaccine and drug
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus, a neurotropic vesiculovirus of Rhabdoviridae, was first isolated in Chandipura, Maharashtra, India (1965). It drives recurring pediatric acute encephalitis outbreaks in India, with case fatality 28–79% across seven outbreaks (2003–2024). The disease primarily affects children under 15, starting with fever and progressing to convulsions, coma or death. Notable outbreaks include 2003 Andhra Pradesh and later events in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha and Bihar; a Gujarat cluster involved 148 cases with 51 laboratory-confirmed infections. There are no approved antivirals or licensed vaccines. A Discover Viruses review (Feb 27, 2026) evaluates laboratory models, concluding mice—especially neonatal/juvenile—have powered the understanding of tropism, immune responses, and pathogenesis, while other species are underused. Neonatal/young mice show age-dependent susceptibility; CNS invasion peaks around 72 hours; seroconversion IgM by 48 hours, with no detectable IgG; passive antibodies provide protection. BBB maturation may underlie age differences.

article.articleHeadline: Bioinformatics pipelines race to outsmart multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major global health challenge, with an estimated 10.7 million new TB cases and 1.23 million deaths in 2024, and India accounting for ~25% of the global burden. The Beni-Suef University Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences (Aug 31, 2026) review argues that computational biology is central to understanding resistance and guiding drug discovery. Resistance arises via chromosomal mutations: rpoB (rifampicin), katG/inhA (isoniazid), gyrA/gyrB (fluoroquinolones), rrs/eis/tlyA (second-line injectables); plus altered permeability, efflux, metabolic adaptation. Extensively drug-resistant TB has further poor prognosis. ML models trained on genomic data achieve >96% accuracy for first-line resistance and detect noncanonical mechanisms. For isoniazid, S315T in KatG destabilizes the heme radical; EmbB mutations alter ligand binding for ethambutol. A discovery pipeline uses subtractive genomics, KEGG/DrugBank, AutoDock/Schrödinger, AlphaFold, MD, and ML scoring with ADMET. A DrugBank screen yielded two repurposed drugs, aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin, active against H37Rv.

article.articleHeadline: Caper Flower Extract Shows Antioxidant and Vibrio-Killing Power in Lab
article.articleSummary: Capparis zeylanica flower methanolic extract (CZFM E; CZFME) shows antioxidant activity (DPPH IC50 57.87 μg/mL) and inhibits pathogenic Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio harveyi (MIC 62.5 μg/mL) in vitro. Flowers collected from Adikavi Nannaya University campus were shade-dried seven days, extracted with methanol (25 g powder, 300 mL) in Soxhlet cycles, yielding 11.2% crude extract. CZFME underwent qualitative phytochemical screening and quantitative polyphenol assessment (79.70 mg gallic acid equivalents per g dry extract). FTIR indicated carboxyl, hydroxyl/phenolic, ester and amide groups; GC-MS identified 27 volatile compounds (cycloheptane derivatives, epoxides, fatty acid esters); LC-MS/MS tentatively identified 61 metabolites spanning flavonoids, coumarins, terpenoids, acids, glycosides, alkaloids. Notable flavonoids include quercetin and kaempferol; alkaloids such as tropane derivatives; terpenoids like bisabolene. Some non-natural compounds were flagged as potential contamination. article.articleHeadline: Risk of PPR disease in goats during winter: identify symptoms and take preventive measures.
article.articleSummary: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) threatens goats in Bhilwara, Rajasthan, India during winter. The disease spreads rapidly between goats; timely recognition and vaccination are crucial. Symptoms include high fever, nasal and ocular discharge, oral ulcers, diarrhea, weakness, coughing, and breathing difficulties; dehydration may follow. Young and weak animals are at higher risk. Transmission occurs via direct contact, contaminated water or feed, and discharges from affected animals. Management tips: immediately isolate symptomatic goats, use separate feeding and drinking utensils, and avoid mixing with healthy animals. Ensure clean, dry, well-ventilated housing; regularly clean the shelter; quarantine new goats before introduction. Vaccination, under veterinary guidance, is the most effective preventive measure; contact the local veterinary department if an outbreak is suspected.

article.articleHeadline: Trichy corporation launches oil ball drive to curtail mosquito menace
article.articleSummary: Trichy city, Tamil Nadu, is stepping up anti-larval mosquito control despite a dry spell following the northeast monsoon. The municipality is deploying oil balls—sawdust soaked in malaria oil, formed into balls and wrapped in old rags—to create a thin oil film on water in inundated vacant plots, suffocating mosquito larvae. About 20,000 vacant plots exist citywide, with current coverage in E Pudur and Karumandapam as residents report increased mosquito nuisance. Officials stress plot owners’ accountability for hygiene, while residents call for pan-city enforcement. Additional measures include spraying Bt bacteria on stagnant water and fogging with pyrethrin in densely populated areas. Fogging equipment includes hand foggers (10 per zone), vehicle-mounted foggers (1 per zone), and portable foggers (15–20 per zone). Vacant-plot distribution: Zone IV 37%, Zone V 31%, Zone III 16%, Zone II 10%, Zone I 6%. No case/death counts are provided.

article.articleHeadline: 25-30 yellow wagtails found dead along Koyna riverbank in Karad
article.articleSummary: About 25-30 yellow wagtails were found dead along the Koyna riverbank in Karad, Kolhapur district, Maharashtra. Samples from the birds have been sent to NIHSAD, Bhopal, and NIV, Pune, under central government guidelines, with results expected in 3–4 days to determine whether deaths were due to an infectious disease (including avian influenza), another viral infection, or an environmental factor. The Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) alerted authorities; BNHS member Rohan Bhate said yellow wagtails are migratory winter visitors, and the incident raises concern for regional migratory bird populations. No other bird species were reported dead nearby; about 5–6 birds were washed away by river flow. Investigators aim to establish whether this is an isolated event or signals a wider zoonotic threat.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Cases Rising in Adilabad District Due to Poor Sanitation
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases rise to 121 in Adilabad district since January 2026 amid poor sanitation and mosquito menace, with Adilabad Municipality bearing the highest burden. Mancherial district reports 17 dengue-positive cases, including 10 Hyderabad-origin students who fell ill in the state capital and returned home. Monthly counts: 47 cases in October, 48 in September, 20 in August; urban PHCs Ankoli, Putlibowli, and Shantinagar account for 69 cases. Symptoms include high fever and decreased platelets, with blood tests confirming dengue. Integrated Disease Surveillance teams collect samples from PHCs and forward them for ELISA confirmation at government institutes. Allegations persist that some Health department officials hide dengue-positive cases, as official confirmation relies on ELISA. Patients are regularly admitted at RIMS, Adilabad, recovering in 3–4 days; no critical cases have been reported yet.

article.articleHeadline: Sambhal News: Municipal Council and Health Department Swing into Action Following Dengue-Chikungunya Complaints.
article.articleSummary: Dengue and Chikungunya complaints trigger action by Sambhal Municipal Council and Health Department. On Friday, the council conducted fogging and sanitation drives, while the health department held a screening camp. Dr. Diksha and team tested about 25 patients; all results were negative, providing relief, with medicines distributed. Subhash Valmiki reported concerns to the executive officer; residents say others in the colony—Alok Saran (admitted at Saini Hospital, Moradabad), Rakhi, Navin, Sahil, Vipin Kumar, and Ayan—are suffering from typhoid and viral fever. They demand regular fogging and cleaning to curb mosquitoes. Drainage issues persist on Badayun Road main street, leading to waterlogging; no drain has been constructed yet. Sanitation inspector Priyanka Singh noted ongoing cleaning, and residents Mustafa, Sachin, Sunita, and Madhu were present; calls for permanent solutions and proactive surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Dhanbad News: Blood samples from 300 people were taken under the filariasis eradication campaign.
article.articleSummary: Filariasis eradication campaign conducted in Ramnagar Gadh, Telamacho Panchayat, Dhanbad district, under Baghmara Community Health Center. A night blood survey collected 300 samples from Oct 28–30, 2026, with 100 samples on the final day at the Ramnagar Gadh camp. All samples will be tested in a laboratory, and patients will receive treatment if infection is confirmed. Night sampling aligns with the nocturnal activity of filarial parasites to ensure accurate detection. The effort, directed by the district commissioner, reflects ongoing public health surveillance to curb transmission of lymphatic filariasis and to promptly manage positive cases. This campaign highlights nocturnal surveillance for vector-borne disease and ongoing efforts to strengthen local diagnostic capacity.

article.articleHeadline: Nearly 8 in 10 Tested U.S. Typhoid Cases Were Not Susceptible to Ciprofloxacin, a Longtime First-Line Antibiotic
article.articleSummary: 78.4% of U.S. typhoid samples (2016–2020) were not susceptible to ciprofloxacin; paratyphoid A non-susceptibility was 94.2%. In a CDC-led analysis of 2,342 enteric fever cases from 47 states, 1,635 bacterial isolates were tested via NARMS. Most cases were travel-related: over 80% had traveled or lived outside the U.S. within 30 days before illness, with India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh as primary destinations. About 5,700 enteric fever cases occur in the U.S. annually; ~8 million worldwide. Ceftriaxone resistance reached 5.5%, largely among travelers to Pakistan. An XDR typhoid outbreak began in Pakistan in 2016; 11 of 67 XDR cases had no reported international travel. The study emphasizes susceptibility-guided therapy, travel history, and testing; vaccines offer partial protection, and azithromycin and meropenem remain options for XDR cases. Typhoid symptoms include fever, fatigue, headache, loss of appetite, and stomach pain, with blood cultures confirming infection and guiding antibiotic choice.

article.articleHeadline: People up to 59 years old have until Saturday to receive the ACWY meningococcal vaccine in Rio de Janeiro.
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro extends Meningococcal ACWY vaccination to residents up to 59 years old through Saturday, Oct 31, 2026, as part of a citywide campaign. The ACWY vaccine protects against four serogroups of Neisseria meningitidis, the bacteria that can cause meningococcal disease, presenting as meningitis or meningococcemia in children and adults. The vaccine has long been available for ages 1–24 and health workers; under Brazil’s SUS, it was incorporated in 2020 for adolescents 11–14 and in 2025 for children 1–4. The October expansion aims to optimize vaccine stocks. The shot is offered at all 245 vaccination clinics, including three extended-hour units of the Super Centro Carioca de Vacinação: Botafogo (Rua General Severiano, 91; daily 8:00–22:00), Zona Norte (Nova América Shopping, Del Castilho) and Zona Oeste (ParkShoppingCampoGrande).

article.articleHeadline: CNA participates in an international forum on foot-and-mouth disease surveillance
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease dominates the International TAFS Forum in Foz do Iguaçu, Paraná, on October 28–29, 2026, where CNA joined seven regional participants and international bodies to discuss prevention, surveillance, and protection of livestock. Attendees from Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Colombia, Chile and Venezuela, along with FAO, the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Panaftosa, and IICA, advanced regional collaboration. Key topics included progress on the Regional Antigen Bank for Foot-and-Mouth Disease (Banvaco), public-private partnerships in eradication and surveillance, contingency planning, and the importance of herd traceability and rapid communication. Emphasis was placed on quick detection, rapid diagnostics, and notification to the official veterinary service for suspected cases. CNA’s João Paulo Franco highlighted plans with Panaftosa to train technicians to advise producers and support rapid response. The forum reinforced regional resilience against FMD.

article.articleSummary: Dengue fever remains a concern in 2026 despite a decline in cases. Health authorities warn that the drop does not mean the threat has ended, and a new surge could occur, particularly as different dengue virus serotypes circulate. The piece signals that the viral landscape is shifting, underscoring the need for continued attention to dengue in the ongoing year, without offering specific geographic or numeric data.

article.articleHeadline: UFPI study identifies the visceral leishmaniasis vector species in Teresina.
article.articleSummary: Visceral leishmaniasis vector Lutzomyia longipalpis detected in Teresina, Piauí, Brazil, by UFPI researchers. In two rural areas, Cacimba Velha (1,243 specimens) and Terra Nossa (108), a total of 1,351 phlebotomine sandflies were captured between August and December 2025, totaling 324 hours of sampling. While vector presence indicates potential exposure, transmission requires integration with data on the parasite, animals, and human cases. The study also tested a low-cost JD2R trap against CDC and HP models; results suggest the prototype needs improvements before broader use in entomological surveillance. The project, led by Karynne Araújo Costa under UFPI's Biodiversity and Conservation program (supervised by Maria Regiane Araújo Soares), builds on Teresina’s longstanding visceral leishmaniasis history dating back to the 1980s and notes vector adaptation to different city environments.

article.articleHeadline: Itapeva records more than 2,600 cases of gastroenteritis and investigates water contamination
article.articleSummary: Itapeva, interior São Paulo, reports a gastroenteritis outbreak with over 2,600 cases in 20 days. Investigations point to potential water contamination after Adolfo Lutz laboratory detected Cryptosporidium in two water samples collected Oct 19 in a central-area square, and clinical tests found enteroaggregative Escherichia coli in patients. While not yet confirmed that the municipal water supply caused the outbreak, authorities suspended municipal and state school classes on Oct 29 and opened a 90-day Special Inquiry Commission to probe water quality and supply failures. Sabesp reported 227 samples (Oct 1–27) met potable standards; new analyses and expanded network monitoring underway. Emergency water deliveries began, with potable water trucks to health facilities and schools; over 40,000 bottles of 2.5% sodium hypochlorite distributed. Citizens advised to boil water at least five minutes before consumption or oral care. Gastroenteritis symptoms include diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, cramps, fever; dehydration warning signs. Investigation ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: Rotary Family mobilizes the Frontier in the fight against poliomyelitis - A Plateia Journal
article.articleSummary: On World Polio Day, October 31, the Rotary Family of Livramento and Rivera mobilizes border communities in the international End Polio Now campaign with a bi-national walk starting at 10:00 from General Osório Square, Sant'Ana do Livramento (Brazil), and Artigas Square, Rivera (Uruguay). Participants will meet at International Park to continue activities organized by Rotary clubs, Rotaract, Interact, and the Rotary Community Development Core. After the walk, the event includes distribution of polio information materials, food sales, health and well-being services, and fundraising for polio eradication. Polio is an infectious disease that can cause paralysis, especially in children; vaccination is the main preventive measure. The Rotary Family invites residents of the Peace Border to join at International Park and support the polio fight.

article.articleHeadline: Food and Veterinary Agency recalls Brazilian chicken due to Salmonella.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-30, Kosovo's Food and Veterinary Agency (AHV) banned sale and ordered withdrawal of frozen chicken meat imported from Brazil after detecting Salmonella Minnesota in samples tied to the private operator Apetit SHPK. Based on laboratory results and the Food Law, AHV imposed a temporary distribution ban, placed the products under official supervision, and initiated a market recall. Salmonella Minnesota in food can cause gastrointestinal infections through consumption or cross-contamination during handling and preparation. Emergency inspections are underway, including verification of the entire imported quantity—from entry into Kosovo to sale—assessment of distributed stocks versus remaining inventory, checks of labels, production and expiry dates, veterinary certificates, and storage conditions, plus additional laboratory analyses. The Agency will oversee measures and, based on risk assessment, decide final disposition, potentially destruction. The public will be informed of results to protect consumer health.

article.articleHeadline: Spreading Rabies Prevention Knowledge from Schools to the Community.
article.articleSummary: Rabies prevention education is being scaled in Vietnam through Boehringer Ingelheim’s STOP Rabies initiative in 2026, expanding from Tay Ninh to Đồng Tháp. The program targets early learning, teaching children safe interactions with dogs and cats, recognizing bite/scratch risks, and appropriate post-exposure actions, underscoring that rabies is fatal once symptoms appear but risk is reduced by vaccinating animals, controlling sources, and timely prophylaxis. Using a Train-the-Trainer model, it equips teachers and school health staff with foundational knowledge and communication skills, plus age-appropriate educational materials to reinforce lessons at home. After 2025 activities in Tay Ninh, the expansion aims to reach over 65,000 elementary and middle school students. In 2026, 116 educators in Tay Ninh and 124 in Đồng Tháp will be trained, totaling 240 personnel to support school-based rabies prevention and community awareness toward eventual elimination.

article.articleHeadline: Five Neighborhoods Commended for Outstanding Dengue Fever Prevention and Control
article.articleSummary: As of October 30, 2026, Taiwan reports 228 confirmed dengue fever cases nationwide, with 214 imported (over 90%), infection sources predominantly from Vietnam. In Tainan City, the cross-agency dengue prevention group held its ninth meeting chaired by Deputy Secretary-General Lin Rong-chuan, reviewing the outbreak and prevention readiness. Five communities were commended for September’s prevention efforts: Chongxing Li, North District; Ping’an Li, Anping District; Shangding Li, Yongkang District; Yutian Li, Yujing District; and Lingzhaoliao Li, Jiangjun District. Dr. Huang Jingji of the NHRI’s Center for Mosquito-Borne Disease Control cautioned that risk persists into autumn-winter and rainfall could boost vector density. Dengue Prevention Center Director Li Cuifeng outlined common symptoms—fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia, nausea, vomiting, and rash—and urged travelers returning from Southeast Asia to seek prompt medical care within two weeks and disclose travel history for early diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Newcastle disease: 37 territories restricted imports of Brazilian poultry after an outbreak in Santa Catarina.
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease outbreak in Santa Catarina, Brazil, led to 37 territories restricting poultry imports: 27 jurisdictions within Santa Catarina, 7 for the state, and 3 for the entire country. Restrictions followed detection of a Newcastle disease focus at a turkey processing plant in Santa Catarina. Brazil’s Ministry of Agriculture (Mapa), with the Foreign Affairs Ministry (MRE), expanded sanitary regionalization to limit trade disruption, in line with OIE guidelines. As of 30 October 2026, the focus identified in Nova Itaberaba prompted localized restrictions; the regionalization is estimated to have avoided about US$954 million in potential annual losses versus 2024 scenarios. Markets with the largest avoided losses include China (~US$485 million), Saudi Arabia (~US$293 million), and Argentina (~US$57 million). Other contributing partners include South Africa, Jordan, Cuba, Egypt, and Vietnam, helping preserve poultry trade for Brazil’s non-affected regions.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 5,000 deaths, WHO warns of the risk of transmission.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 deaths as of October 30, 2026, with total cases exceeding 10,000 since the May 2026 start, making it the deadliest Ebola wave in the country and the second-largest globally after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo virus strain; there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain. By October 28, the World Health Organization counted 10,274 laboratory-confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths, though Congolese officials note higher death counts due to data timing. Eight of 26 provinces have reported cases, concentrated in Ituri (over 7,300 cases, >3,400 deaths) and North Kivu (≈2,400 cases, >1,300 deaths). Cross-border spillover includes Uganda, Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths by Oct 26), Nigeria (Abuja, linked to Uganda), and treatment in Switzerland; imported/exported cases do not imply sustained transmission. Vietnam is strengthening border surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Pretomanid resistance found in 4.5% of tuberculosis isolates in China
article.articleSummary: China-wide study of 335 Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from drug-resistance surveillance regions in patients with no prior pretomanid exposure found a baseline pretomanid resistance rate of 4.5% (15/335). In Middlebrook 7H9 broth, the 99th percentile MIC was 0.25 mg/L, with resistant isolates showing MICs from 0.5 mg/L to ≥16 mg/L. Genetic analysis showed mutations in fbiA, fbiC, or fgd1 in only 3 of the 15 resistant isolates; none had mutations in fbiB, ddn, or fbiD, implying uncharacterized resistance mechanisms beyond established markers. The dataset is predominantly lineage 2 (77.9%), and the 99th percentile MIC applies to both lineage 2 and lineage 4 in China. The findings indicate phenotypic resistance can exist without known mutations, highlighting limitations of molecular assays and providing MIC-distribution data to support ECOFFs and clinical breakpoints for broth microdilution in China. For interpretation, isolates with MIC ≥0.5 mg/L may be considered probably resistant.

article.articleHeadline: Newly isolated feline coronavirus strain AH2023 proves lethal in cats
article.articleSummary: AH2023 is a newly characterized feline coronavirus type II (FCoV-II) isolated from a cat in Hefei, Anhui Province, eastern China. In experimental infections, all young cats developed feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) and died within roughly 17–19 days post exposure, underscoring the virulence of FCoV-II. The virus was recovered from ascitic fluid of a British Shorthair with FIP and confirmed as FCoV-II after three blind passages in CRFK cells, with Western blot and RT-PCR. Genome sequencing (29,013 nt; 11 open reading frames) places AH2023 with Chinese type II strains SH2021 and DQ2023; recombination analysis shows the first ~13 kb most similar to type I SD, and the region 13,335–26,006 with canine coronavirus HLJ-072 and TGEV P115, breakpoint near 13 kb. Spike gene (nucleotides 20,436–24,800; 1,454 aa) shares 91.4–99.9% identity with type II; an S829F substitution may influence pathogenicity. GenBank accession PX471051.1.

article.articleHeadline: Hookworm Prevalence Fell Sharply in Rural China After Integrated Control
article.articleSummary: Hookworm infection in six rural villages of Tiantai County, Zhejiang Province, China, declined after a one-year integrated control program combining sanitation, health education, deworming, and village-level management. Baseline 2022 stool surveys showed 1,218 individuals with 58 positive cases (4.76%). Post-intervention 2024 surveys of 1,222 individuals found 13 infections (1.06%), a 77.73% reduction. Using Firth penalized logistic regression to handle sparse data, adjusted for sex, age, education, occupation, and village, the odds of infection in 2024 were significantly lower than in 2022 (adjusted odds ratio 0.223; 95% CI 0.125–0.399; P < 0.001). Higher odds of infection were linked to male sex, primary education or below, and residence in Qianyang, Xiatang, or Xiaqiao villages, indicating concentrated transmission. Limitations include lack of non-intervention control villages; causal attribution remains associative. Continued surveillance and targeted efforts are needed to push transmission toward elimination.

article.articleHeadline: Gene-Silencing Vector Shows Strong Protection Against Rabies in Mice
article.articleSummary: Rabies virus remains one of the most lethal human pathogens, and once neurological symptoms appear, no effective treatment exists. A new study reports that a gene-silencing approach delivered by recombinant adeno-associated virus serotype 2 (rAAV2) markedly suppresses rabies replication and improves survival in six-week-old Kunming mice challenged with CVS-11. SiRNA constructs targeting the G glycoprotein (si-G997) and the L polymerase (si-L5055) reduced viral replication in cell lines, lowered G/L mRNA and protein levels, and decreased viral titers. In vivo, intracerebral delivery of rAAV2 (2×10^11 vg/kg) followed by intramuscular CVS-11 challenge yielded 90% survival for pretreatment groups and 88.9% survival postexposure for both vectors, vs ~55% in controls. Brain viral loads were reduced at day 7 in treated groups, indicating a broad therapeutic window. Published 2026-10-30 in Animal Diseases.

article.articleHeadline: Mycoplasma pneumoniae in hospitalized children: 20-year study finds age
article.articleSummary: Mycoplasma pneumoniae remains a stable, cyclical driver of pediatric respiratory illness in eastern China. In a 20-year retrospective study of 51,399 hospitalized children under 18 (2005–2025) at Soochow University affiliated hospitals, 16,086 tested positive (31.3% overall). Epidemics wax and wane every 3–5 years, with peaks during 2008–2009, 2013, and 2016. Age is the consistent infection determinant: positivity rises with age—≥7 years 51.73%, 3–7 years 41.04%, 1–3 years 34.13%, 6–12 months 24.80%, <6 months 12.97%. In 2021–2025, older children accounted for a larger share of cases. COVID-19 measures cut positivity to 22.42–25.58% (2020–2022), especially in >7 years (67.49% to 42.49%) and 3–7 years (54.36% to 26.74%). Younger children also showed reduced positivity, though magnitude smaller. A 2023 rebound to 45.16% preceded a 2024–2025 decline. Summer remained a peak season; autumn declined in most recent period. Female children were consistently more often positive (35.47% vs 28.61%). Limitations: observational, positivity from tested specimens.

article.articleHeadline: Machine Learning Flags Airway Cast Risk in Children With Mycoplasma
article.articleSummary: In Shaanxi, China, a single-center retrospective study of 702 hospitalized children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia who underwent fiberoptic bronchoscopy (Jan 2023–Jan 2026) found 225 with plastic bronchitis (PB) and 477 without. The goal was to flag PB risk early using admission data; eight models were trained and two web-based calculators released. Nine predictors from within 24 hours of admission were selected: fever duration, peak temperature, white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, albumin, lactate dehydrogenase, fibrinogen degradation products, D-dimer, and pulmonary consolidation. On the independent test set, Random Forest achieved an accuracy of 0.853, F1 0.759, and ROC-AUC 0.881, while CatBoost reached 0.853 accuracy and ROC-AUC 0.871. Some overfitting was noted. The cohort is bronchoscopy-selected, so PB proportion does not reflect incidence in unselected patients. Published 2026-10-30 in Frontiers in Pediatrics.

article.articleHeadline: Horse Parasites in Inner Mongolia Reveal Zoonotic Cryptosporidium Strains
article.articleSummary: In central and western Inner Mongolia, a 325-horse fecal-sample survey (Otog Banner, Ordos City; Zhenglan and Abaga Banners, Xilingol League) collected May–Sept 2025 found Cryptosporidium at 2.8% (9/325) and Enterocytozoon bieneusi at 1.5% (5/325). C. hominis comprised 55.6% of Cryptosporidium positives (5/9) and C. parvum 44.4% (4/9); Otog Banner showed all C. parvum positives (6.7%), Zhenglan Banner all C. hominis and all E. bieneusi positives (4.1%), Abaga Banner none. C. hominis gp60 subtypes: IkA18G1 (4 isolates) and IkA19G1 (1, newly reported in Inner Mongolia); Ik family linked to humans, indicating zoonotic potential. No gp60 data were obtained for C. parvum. All E. bieneusi sequences were genotype horse1 (Group 1; Hap_1). Foals ≤1 year had higher Cryptosporidium prevalence (11.5%) versus adults (1.1%); diarrheic horses 16.1% vs 1.4% in non-diarrheic. Findings published in Frontiers in Veterinary Science, data collected May–Sept 2025.

article.articleHeadline: Viktor Orbán may get a chance after controversial UN Secretaries-General: Nazi past, wartime crisis, cholera outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Viktor Orbán may get a chance to lead the United Nations, per The Wall Street Journal citing three diplomatic sources that he could be the next Secretary-General. Backing from the United States, Russia, and China is reported, but the nomination requires at least nine of the 15 Security Council members to support it, and no veto may be cast. Orbán would only run if confident no one would oppose him. Past secretaries-general are linked with various crises and outbreaks: Kurt Waldheim’s post revealed Wehrmacht service; Javier Pérez de Cuéllar presided during Iran–Iraq war, Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, and the 1982 Lebanon War. Boutros-Ghali faced the 1994 Rwandan genocide and the 1995 Srebrenica massacre. Kofi Annan’s tenure was marred by the Oil-for-Food Programme abuses. Ban Ki-moon’s era saw a cholera outbreak in Haiti tied to UN peacekeepers. António Guterres faced investigations into alleged UNRWA staff involvement in the 2023 Hamas attack.

article.articleHeadline: FEHD announces October's fourth batch of Aedes albopictus mosquito trap indices.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-30, Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) released the October fourth batch of Aedes albopictus ovitrap indices, part of ongoing efforts to curb dengue fever and chikungunya. The department maintains 62 surveillance districts where ovitraps are placed for two weeks, with weekly collections to derive ovitrap and density indices. Through cross-department collaboration, district vector-control task forces, and risk-based targeting in areas with heavy mosquito activity, FEHD conducts intensified inspections, eliminates breeding sites, applies larvicides, fogging to kill adults, and adds traps as needed. Public education campaigns and a rapid notification system keep estates and residents alert. Citizens are urged to remove standing water, inspect containers (garbage bins, flower pots, air-conditioning bases, drying racks), refresh water in vases weekly, and cover water-holding items. Indices and prevention data are available on FEHD channels.

article.articleHeadline: Baby Matthew critically ill with influenza A stranded in Hong Kong as family seeks private air transfer to UK
article.articleSummary: Baby Matthew, from Nottinghamshire, is critically ill in Hong Kong with influenza A after three cardiac arrests; he is ventilated and unable to travel home by commercial flight, prompting a private air transfer arranged by Lia's Wings. The family seeks a donated long-haul aircraft to fly to the UK for NHS tests and treatment; estimated cost up to £200,000 for a dedicated air ambulance, beyond family and charity means. A specialist team (two consultants and a paediatric nurse) and equipment to adapt the jet are on standby, with both Hong Kong and English clinicians agreeing on the plan. Without repatriation, Matthew faces gradual medical decline away from home support. Travel insurance excludes repatriation. Lia's Wings notes rising demand for pediatric international transfers, assisting 68 children in six months of 2026, and over 300 since 2010. Hong Kong health authorities had warned of rising seasonal influenza A activity and urged vigilance.

article.articleHeadline: Op-Ed| Why communities must be at the center of Ebola preparedness and response in South Sudan - Radio Tamazuj
article.articleSummary: Ebola preparedness in South Sudan centers on Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) to bridge technical readiness and community action. With ongoing regional threat from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)—10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths as of 25 October 2026—and Kenya reporting 9 cases and 2 deaths as of 26 October, cross-border movement into South Sudan raises risk, notably over 5,000 people entering through Ibba County in Western Equatoria between July and mid-October. South Sudan’s preparedness includes surveillance, laboratory readiness, infection prevention and control, points-of-entry measures, and simulated exercises in Juba, Yei, and Yambio, plus a national toll-free line (6666) for suspected case reporting. RCCE involves faith leaders, community frontline actors, and media professionals to build trust, proximity, and reach; they reinforce accurate prevention messages, encourage early reporting and care-seeking, and counter misinformation amid Ebola outbreaks in the region.

article.articleHeadline: DRC: The epidemiological situation of tuberculosis remains concerning (National Tuberculosis Control Program) - ACP
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa, 30 October 2026 – The epidemiological situation of tuberculosis (TB) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains concerning despite progress in detection, notification, and care. Gains include expanded diagnostic capacity with rapid molecular tests (GeneXpert), community engagement, and better access to treatment. However the TB burden remains heavy, especially among children, people living with HIV, the malnourished, residents of remote areas, and those in crowded settings. Key obstacles are insufficient diagnostic equipment, uneven geographic distribution, maintenance problems, and frequent stockouts of antituberculosis medicines. Some clinics lack power or cartridges; patients travel long distances for molecular testing. Delays in diagnosis worsen disease, increase costs and mortality, and prolong transmission. For rifampicin-resistant/multidrug-resistant TB, rapid diagnosis is essential to select appropriate short regimens. Recommendations: boost national TB funding, decentralize diagnostics, secure supplies, strengthen sample transport, and intensify active community screening, including pediatric TB, TB-HIV co-infection, and drug-resistant TB. Dependency on external funding threatens sustainability.

article.articleHeadline: Malaga University discovers method for predicting Ebola outbreaks up to a year in advance | Sur in English
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks across Africa may expand due to climatic teleconnections; a Malaga University (UMA) study predicts outbreaks up to 6-12 months in advance. Using data from 49 African outbreaks (1976–2025) and 26 climate indices, researchers found Ebola emergence linked to large-scale weather patterns rather than random timing. Four indicators drive regional risk: Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) as the most decisive, Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), quasi-biennial oscillation (QBO), and Caribbean Sea surface temperature (CAR). These fluctuations alter rainfall and ecology, creating conditions favorable for wildlife-human spillover. Lead time of six to twelve months enables targeted surveillance and preparedness in high-risk zones. The Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported over 8,000 confirmed Ebola cases and around 3,901 deaths (case fatality ~50%). Authors aim to develop an integrated monitoring system combining macroclimate, local meteorology, deforestation, and wildlife biogeography for early detection.

article.articleHeadline: Antibodies in people vaccinated against smallpox neutralize monkeypox.
article.articleSummary: American molecular biologists, led by Ian Wilson of the Scripps Research Institute, identified in a library of monoclonal antibodies from people vaccinated against smallpox in the 1990s 33 antibodies that bind MPXV proteins A35 and B6, which drive the virus’s two major forms. Most antibodies target the same region on A35 and neutralize related orthopoxvirus peptides, indicating a broad action. When two antibodies, A35-Ab17 and B6-Ab15, were given to mpox-infected mice, each protected about 75% of animals, while their combination prevented death in all treated mice. The study, published in Science Immunology, suggests a two-antibody therapy or prophylaxis against monkeypox. MPXV drew global attention after large outbreaks in 2022–2024 (roughly 93,000 cases and 208 deaths), with subsequent flare-ups in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and other Central African states. VACV-based smallpox vaccines were used worldwide until the early 1980s.

article.articleHeadline: Outcry Over Discovery of Listeria Bacteria in Enoki Mushrooms: Here’s the Ideal Way to Cook Them.
article.articleSummary: Five raw enoki mushroom samples bought from five Bangkok shops tested positive for Listeria monocytogenes, detected by Thailand’s National Institute of Food Safety in both domestic and China-origin production. Although the small sample size limits breadth, the finding reiterates food-safety concerns surrounding enoki mushrooms, often used in hotpots and stir-fries. Listeria infection (listeriosis) can cause fever, headache, muscle pain, diarrhea, and vomiting; while most healthy individuals recover, older adults, pregnant women, and immunocompromised persons face higher risk of invasive disease such as bloodstream infection or meningitis, with pregnancy risk including miscarriage or preterm birth. Listeria can grow at refrigeration temperatures, so cold storage isn’t protective. In May 2026, the U.S. FDA recalled enoki products and imposed import restrictions from China and Korea. Thai guidance calls for cooking mushrooms to at least 74°C (boiling or sautéing for several minutes), keeping raw separate from cooked foods, and sanitizing surfaces; CDC urges restaurants not to serve raw enoki or use as garnish.

article.articleHeadline: Floods Drive Leptospirosis Outbreaks in Southeast Asia, Review Finds
article.articleSummary: Floods drive leptospirosis outbreaks in Southeast Asia; eight studies (Malaysia 3, Indonesia 2, Thailand 2, Philippines 1) published 2020–2025 link monsoon rains, typhoons, and tropical cyclones to outbreaks with a consistent 1–3 month lag, creating an operational window for warnings and protective measures. Environmental drivers include rainfall volume, stagnant surface water, humidity, and river overflow; inadequate drainage in Malaysia expands flood-risk zones and supports persistent contamination. Social factors such as direct rodent contact, handling contaminated food, wading through floodwaters, skin wounds, male gender, and lack of PPE elevate risk; Indonesian case-control data highlight higher odds in flood-prone households with stagnant water and wounds. Temporal patterns show Indonesia after Tropical Cyclone Cempaka; Philippines after typhoons; Malaysia peaks with monsoons; Thailand modeling shows floods amplify transmission. Study designs span cross-sectional, ecological, mixed-methods, and case-control; heterogeneity precludes meta-analysis; protective strategies—including warnings and protective equipment—are identified as promising.

article.articleHeadline: Fever and Chills Could Be Symptoms of Malaria; Recognize Other Signs.
article.articleSummary: Malaria, caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by mosquito bites, remains a major health challenge in Indonesia and globally. As of July 2026, Indonesia reported 346,866 malaria cases, while global cases reached about 282 million in 2024 with 610,000 deaths. Early symptoms mimic flu and include fever with chills, headache, muscle aches, and fatigue; more severe disease can cause shortness of breath, seizures, jaundice, and dark urine. Symptoms may appear days to a month after infection, and in some cases even after a year. Transmission can also occur during pregnancy, transfusion, organ donation, or shared needles. Prevention focuses on avoiding mosquito bites via DEET repellents, covering skin, and bed nets, especially when traveling to endemic regions; chemoprophylaxis may be prescribed. Diagnosis uses blood tests to detect Plasmodium species; treatment relies on antimalarial drugs, with early treatment reducing severe complications.

article.articleHeadline: From Wallace to vaccines: Indonesia seeks homegrown malaria solutions
article.articleSummary: Indonesia aims to accelerate development of a domestically produced malaria vaccine to address Plasmodium vivax, which causes a significant share of malaria in Southeast Asia and is prevalent in Papua. By 2026, about 80% of districts and cities are malaria-free, with 95% of remaining cases in Papua. In 2025 the Health Ministry recorded 706,297 malaria cases, aided by active case detection and digital reporting. After a Oct 27 cabinet meeting, BRIN head Arif Satria said President Prabowo urged acceleration; BRIN, Health Ministry, and Bio Farma plan to shorten development by three years, aligning trials, BPOM reviews, and production planning toward elimination by 2030. World Health Organization–recommended vaccines RTS,S and R21 target P. falciparum; no approved vaccine for P. vivax exists. Papua region has long faced P. vivax—Timika (2004–2005) showed 37% of confirmed cases due to P. vivax, with chloroquine resistance identified in 1989 and MDR linked to severe malaria in children.

article.articleHeadline: Sorong Health Office evaluates the malaria control program - ANTARA News Central Papua
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Sorong Regency, Southwest Papua, Indonesia rose to 1,327 cases in 2026, prompting evaluation of the malaria prevention and control program. The head of Disease Prevention and Control, Agustinus Wabia, said the review involves primary health centers, hospitals, and private clinics to validate data and identify implementation obstacles. Sorong remains a high-endemic area with transmission concentrated in Aimas District (Klabinain, Maibo villages), Mayamuk District (Kampung Jeflio, Arar), Mega District, Salawati Selatan, and Seget. The program prioritizes case finding, testing, and treatment monitoring, alongside vector control and community empowerment. Plans include mass bed net distribution to high-burden villages, with routine nets provided to patients and pregnant women. Fogging is under study and not yet implemented due to the need for community education and alignment with mosquito activity (around 18:00 WIT); larval source management and drain cleaning continue. The evaluation aims to strengthen cross-sector coordination and improve control effectiveness.

article.articleHeadline: 85 Percent of Jembrana's Rabies-Transmitting Animals Have Been Vaccinated Against Rabies, in an Effort to Curb Rabies Cases in Jembrana.
article.articleSummary: Rabies vaccination campaign in Jembrana, Bali, Indonesia, is intensifying to curb rabies cases. By mid-October 2026, 34,129 rabies-transmitting animals (HPR) have been vaccinated: 31,397 dogs, 2,171 cats, and 21 monkeys, reaching 85% coverage. Although cases are down this year, 81 rabies-positive cases have been reported across multiple districts, underscoring ongoing risk due to rapid transmission. Vaccination efforts focus both in residential areas and high-risk dumping sites such as beaches and rivers where unowned animals are discarded, a potential source of new outbreaks. The program is led by the Jembrana Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food. Authorities urge residents with unvaccinated pets to have them vaccinated and to report HPR to health officials to sustain control and prevent spillovers from stray dogs.

article.articleHeadline: Nagan Raya Regency Health Office completes integrated TB tracing CKG at 26 locations.
article.articleSummary: In Nagan Raya Regency, Aceh, Indonesia, the Health Office completed an integrated tuberculosis tracing program with Free Health Checks (CKG) at 26 sites, with Gampong Uteun Pulo in Seunagan Timur as the final location in 2026. Conducted with the district health office (Dinkes) and all Puskesmas, the effort screened over 3,000 household and close contacts of TB patients, yielding 413 people suspected of tuberculosis. From these, 30 new TB cases were diagnosed, and 150 individuals began tuberculosis preventive therapy. The initiative aims to curb transmission and improve community health, underscoring ongoing public health collaboration and encouraging continued participation, routine health checks, and healthy lifestyles to combat TB and other infectious diseases in the region.

article.articleHeadline: Ghana AIDS Commission Reports Young People Aged 15 to 24 Account for 30% of New HIV Infections
article.articleSummary: In Ghana, young people aged 15-24 account for about 30% of all new HIV infections, the Ghana AIDS Commission reports. Despite ongoing campaigns and educational programmes, this age group remains particularly vulnerable to HIV infection, indicating that prevention efforts require refinement. Contributing factors cited include limited access to accurate information, risky sexual behaviours, and inadequate utilisation of prevention services. The Commission calls for intensified public education, expanded access to testing and counselling, and stronger youth-friendly health programmes that can reach adolescents and young adults. It urges greater involvement of schools, communities, families, and religious institutions to promote awareness and responsible behaviour. Stakeholders in the health sector are urged to prioritise youth-focused strategies and to ensure young people have the knowledge, resources, and support needed to protect themselves, aligning with Ghana's goal of ending the HIV epidemic.
